Prefers Reduced Motion

Someone has the system's reduce motion setting on and my page animations still run. Should I handle it?

Reading the system's reduce motion setting and disabling or reducing animation accordingly·When visitors enable their system's reduced-motion preference, a page can query it and reduce, stop, or replace nonessential animation, such as replacing a large movement with a static state. Keep loading and status information clear; a spinning icon can be replaced with text or progress. Toggle the system setting to check that the page responds.

example.com
Banner background gradient
Card oneCard twoCard three
Loading indicator and decorative motion both running
Reduce motion: off
  • Decorative gradient: shifting slowly
  • Page layout: kept
  • Loading status: spinning cue

These controls simulate the system preference; with it on, the background gradient and spinner stop while the loading state remains readable.

What reduce motion handles

Nonessential animation can change: When the preference is on, reduce, stop, or replace nonessential motion such as large movement or parallax.

Keep the page state clear: You can stop a loading spinner and use text or progress to show that work continues; keeping the information does not require keeping the animation.

Verify with the system setting: After changing it, toggle the system setting once and check whether the page animation actually follows—that is acceptance.

What people often confuse

Reduced motion expresses a preference for less nonessential movement; an implementation can reduce, stop, or replace animation. Whatever the choice, keep the page state clear.
